summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease and a complex medical history was admitted after experiencing acute dizziness, confusion, and gait instability, initially raising concern for stroke. Neurology evaluation ruled out acute stroke, attributing her symptoms to toxic metabolic encephalopathy from missed dialysis, with elevated creatinine and urea. She received two hemodialysis sessions during admission, leading to clinical improvement. Keratitis in the right eye was diagnosed and treated with antibiotic eye drops. Her warfarin dose was increased for subtherapeutic anticoagulation. She was discharged home with home physical therapy, walker assistance, and follow-up plans, with resolution of acute symptoms and stable lab values.
